rect.title: This diagram is drawn from ply.yaml, the file describing this codebase's architecture and verification claims. Each box is a component; chips are functions with their declared checks; arrows are permitted calls (solid) and data flows (dashed); red bars are forbidden calls. A box's grey depth is how strongly it promises to be checked — white means something inside promises nothing, deeper grey means stronger checks promised, and the weakest function sets the whole box's shade. Nothing here is green: green is kept for evidence a run has actually earned, and nothing has been run yet, so a picture full of promises should not look like a picture full of results. Hover anything for its meaning.

g.title: ply.yaml — the document this picture is drawn from. Everything you see here was declared in it; nothing was inferred from code. What each box has actually been checked for is what `cargo ply verify` reports, not this drawing.

What this document declares, before anything has been run. "1 function promises nothing" counts functions with no checks against them at all -- code the diagram is showing you but says nothing about. Running `cargo ply verify` is what turns promises into results; this line never reports results.
`*` stands for every component
no component may call feed — such a call fails the build
`*` stands for every component
no component may call book — except decoder — such a call fails the build

#7 marks an unresolved decision — a question the design still owes an answer: backpressure policy when the ring is full: drop frame vs spin. It belongs to the workspace as a whole, not to any function or component yet; Ply tracks it until someone resolves it (§5.6).

component feed — maps to Rust module ingest::feed capabilities: net no checks are declared anywhere in this component — nothing here is verified yet (unclaimed) this box is white because `Feed::pump` declares no checks at all — one unchecked thing inside sets the shade of everything around it
this component may use `net`. A component may use only the capabilities it declares — using an undeclared one is an architecture finding (§5.3, A0404).
Feed::pump no checks declared — nothing about this function is verified (unclaimed)

component ring — maps to Rust module disruptor::spsc capabilities: unsafe owns disruptor::spsc::Spsc — only this component may mutate them profile hot_path — a named bundle of extra rules this component must follow: no_panics (functions here must never panic (crash on purpose)), exhaustive_match (every match must handle all cases explicitly) declares checks up to bounded — proved for every input up to a loop bound — the strongest verdict this could earn; none of it has been run yet this box is this shade because `Spsc::try_push` is the weakest thing in it: it declares bounded — proved for every input up to a loop bound — nothing here is drawn stronger than its weakest part
this component may use `unsafe`. A component may use only the capabilities it declares — using an undeclared one is an architecture finding (§5.3, A0404).

profile `hot_path` — a named bundle of extra rules this component must follow: no_panics (functions here must never panic (crash on purpose)), exhaustive_match (every match must handle all cases explicitly)
Spsc::try_push bounded(3) — proves the contract for every input, unrolling loops at most 3 times generic — every check ran with T=ingest::feed::RawFrame; the evidence covers only that type
Spsc::try_pop bounded(3) — proves the contract for every input, unrolling loops at most 3 times generic — every check ran with T=ingest::feed::RawFrame; the evidence covers only that type

component decoder — maps to Rust module ingest::decode pure — the double border is the seal: this component declares no capabilities and may not use any; capability use inside it is an error (A0408) profile hot_path — a named bundle of extra rules this component must follow: no_panics (functions here must never panic (crash on purpose)), exhaustive_match (every match must handle all cases explicitly) declares checks up to bounded — proved for every input up to a loop bound — the strongest verdict this could earn; none of it has been run yet this box is this shade because `decode` is the weakest thing in it: it declares bounded — proved for every input up to a loop bound — nothing here is drawn stronger than its weakest part

profile `hot_path` — a named bundle of extra rules this component must follow: no_panics (functions here must never panic (crash on purpose)), exhaustive_match (every match must handle all cases explicitly)

decode bounded(2) — proves the contract for every input, unrolling loops at most 2 times fuzz(4096) — runs the function on 4096 random inputs, checking the contract on each mutate — plants small deliberate bugs; the test/fuzz checks must catch every one, or the contract is flagged weak 1 worked example(s), each compiled into a test

component book — maps to Rust module ingest::book owns ingest::book::OrderBook — only this component may mutate them profile hot_path — a named bundle of extra rules this component must follow: no_panics (functions here must never panic (crash on purpose)), exhaustive_match (every match must handle all cases explicitly) strict — architecture findings inside this component fail the build (errors, not warnings) declares checks up to bounded — proved for every input up to a loop bound — the strongest verdict this could earn; none of it has been run yet this box is this shade because `OrderBook::apply` is the weakest thing in it: it declares bounded — proved for every input up to a loop bound — nothing here is drawn stronger than its weakest part

profile `hot_path` — a named bundle of extra rules this component must follow: no_panics (functions here must never panic (crash on purpose)), exhaustive_match (every match must handle all cases explicitly)

OrderBook::apply bounded(2) — proves the contract for every input, unrolling loops at most 2 times fuzz(256) — runs the function on 256 random inputs, checking the contract on each mutate — plants small deliberate bugs; the test/fuzz checks must catch every one, or the contract is flagged weak
OrderBook::updates bounded(2) — proves the contract for every input, unrolling loops at most 2 times
OrderBook::last_px bounded(2) — proves the contract for every input, unrolling loops at most 2 times
feed -> ring — feed may call ring. An undeclared cross-component call is flagged as an architecture finding — a warning by default, an error if the calling component is `strict` (§5.3, A0402).
decoder -> ring — decoder may call ring. An undeclared cross-component call is flagged as an architecture finding — a warning by default, an error if the calling component is `strict` (§5.3, A0402).
decoder -> book — decoder may call book. An undeclared cross-component call is flagged as an architecture finding — a warning by default, an error if the calling component is `strict` (§5.3, A0402).
RawFrame data flows from feed to ring — declared for the picture; nothing checks flows in v1
RawFrame data flows from ring to decoder — declared for the picture; nothing checks flows in v1
Tick data flows from decoder to book — declared for the picture; nothing checks flows in v1
